name: trip-planning
comment: A fixed multi-turn tool-calling trace. Data, not code, so the thing being
compared across runs is pinned in the repository rather than constructed
Every tool result is a constant, or a constant plus arguments echoed back.
Nothing here reads a clock, a random source, a UUID, or the filesystem: a
stub that varied would make every trace differ and the harness would report
the stub rather than the engine. verify_trace.py re-evaluates each stub a
second time and fails if the two answers differ, rather than trusting this
Echoing arguments back is deliberate. It makes a result depend on the call
that produced it, so a divergence in one turn's arguments propagates into
later turns instead of being absorbed.
system: You are a travel assistant. Use the provided tools to answer. Call one tool at a time.
user: I am flying from London to Paris on 2026-03-14. Check the weather in Paris, then convert 500 GBP to EUR.
_tool_choice: The first turn is forced. tool_choice 'auto' compiles to no grammar at all,
which is the correct OpenAI reading (the model decides), but a 1B model
decides to write prose and the trace ends up with no actions in it. Forcing
turn 0 guarantees the loop has something to be deterministic ABOUT, while
leaving later turns on 'auto' keeps the number of turns a property of the
model rather than of this file.
